before.title: A countable dense subset of the universal development by rational timelike exponential steps from a dense subset of the initial surface
before.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ and the
family of member maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as
in [[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d), so that $Q$ is a
Hausdorff locally Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian
metric $\bar g$, the sets $Q_\alpha$ are open and cover $Q$, and
$\bar j(\Sigma)\subseteq Q$ is the embedded initial surface. Then there is a
countable subset $D\subseteq Q$ with:

**(a)** $D\cap\bar j(\Sigma)$ is dense in $\bar j(\Sigma)$; and

**(b)** $D$ is dense in $Q$.

Moreover $D$ can be chosen of the following explicit form: with
$D_0:=S_0$ a countable dense subset of $\bar j(\Sigma)$, and having chosen
for every $x\in D_n$ a basis $(e_1(x),\dots,e_4(x))$ of $T_xQ$ and defined
$$V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}:=\Bigl\{\sum_{i=1}^4q_ie_i(x):\ q_i\in\mathbb Q\Bigr\},$$
one sets
$$D_{n+1}:=D_n\cup\bigl\{\exp_x(v):\ x\in D_n,\ v\in V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}\text{ timelike, with }\exp_x(v)\text{ defined}\bigr\},\qquad D:=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}D_n.$$

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix the data of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$, a
matter sector with initial data $\psi_0$, and constants $\Lambda,\kappa$.
Write $Z_0:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ and let $j_0:\Sigma\to Z_0$,
$j_0(x):=(x,0)$.

**(a) The set-sized family.** Let $\mathcal X$ be the collection of all
tuples $(U,g,N,\psi)$ such that $U\subseteq Z_0$ is an open neighbourhood of
$j_0(\Sigma)$ in $Z_0$, $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $U$, $N$ a time
orientation and $\psi$ matter fields of the sector on $U$, and
$(U,g,N,j_0,\psi)$ is a development of the data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a). Then
$\mathcal X$ is a set, and it is nonempty provided at least one development
of the data exists.

**(b) Identifications.** For $\alpha=(U_\alpha,g_\alpha,N_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$
and $\beta\in\mathcal X$ let $(U_{\alpha\beta},\varphi_{\alpha\beta})$ be
their maximal common development, regarded as a subset of $U_\alpha$
([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]], [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]];
in the convention of the definition it is realised inside the first member).
Let $Z:=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}U_\alpha$ and let $\sim$ be the
equivalence relation on $Z$ **generated** by the relations
$x\sim\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(x)$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal X$ and
$x\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ (a finite chain of such steps, in either order).
Then the classes of two points $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$ coincide if and
only if $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)$.

**(c) The quotient.** Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi$. Then
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset
$Q_\alpha:=\pi(U_\alpha)$, the family $\{Q_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}$
covers $Q$, and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(d) Structure.** $Q$ is Hausdorff and locally Euclidean and carries a
unique smooth atlas (unique in the sense of maximal atlases compatible with
the charts below) making all maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms onto open
subsets, together with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, a time orientation
$\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ such that every $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ is an
isometry onto its image preserving time orientation and matter fields, and
such that $\bar j:=\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ (independent of $\alpha$) is a
common embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data $(h,K,\psi_0)$. The field
equations hold on $Q$, and every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in
$Q$ meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value. Hence
$(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ satisfies every clause of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a) except possibly
the second countability of the underlying manifold; if $Q$ is second
countable then it is a development of the data.

**(e) Universality.** Every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data
admits a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.

**Data.** Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, so that $\Sigma$ is
Hausdorff, second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$,
let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, and let a **matter sector** be specified
as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a finite list of tensor types
$r_1,\dots,r_s$, a smooth **stress-energy construction** $T(g,\psi)$, a smooth
covariant symmetric $2$-tensor field built from a Lorentzian metric $g$ and
fields $\psi=(\psi^1,\dots,\psi^s)$ of the listed types on a four-manifold
carrying $\Sigma$, and a system $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that in every chart the
combined system for $(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] is a first-order quasilinear
symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on shell. Let smooth **matter initial data**
$\psi_0$ on $\Sigma$ be given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] clause (d) hold on
$\Sigma$, with $n$ the future unit normal and $T$ determined by $(h,K,\psi_0)$.
The concrete sectors used later in this batch are the vacuum sector ($s=0$,
$T=0$), the scalar-field sector ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), the
strict barotropic perfect-fluid sector ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]])
and the geodesic-dust sector ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); no other sector is
asserted here.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. smooth sections $\psi^i$ of the tensor bundles over $M$ of the types
   $r_i$ of the sector;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $\psi_0$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$, so $\varphi$ carries
   the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, that is, $\psi'{}^i(\varphi(p))=(d\varphi_p)^{\otimes}\psi^i(p)$
   for every $i$ and $p$, with the natural action on tensor fields of each
   listed type.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,\psi_0)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

A topological space $X$ is **second countable** when its topology has a basis $\mathcal B$ that is at most countable ([[def-topology-basis-subbasis]], [[def-countable]]). Thus every open set is a union of members of one at most countable family $\mathcal B$.

Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, let $F:M\to N$ be a map, let $p\in M$ and
let $r\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$.
For $m,q\in\mathbb N_0$ and an open set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, a map
$g:E\to\mathbb R^q$ is **of class $C^r$** as follows. When $m=0$, every such
map is declared $C^r$. When $m\ge1$, each component $g_l$ with $l<q$ must be
$C^r$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]; when $q=0$ this
component condition is vacuous.
Suppose $F$ is continuous at $p$. Then $F$ is **of class $C^r$ at $p$** when
there are smooth charts $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ at $p$ and $(V,\psi)$ of $N$ at
$F(p)$ with $F(U)\subseteq V$ such that the coordinate representative

$$\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(U)\longrightarrow\psi(V)$$

([[def-coordinate-representation-of-a-map]]) is of class $C^r$ on a
neighbourhood of $\varphi(p)$ in this componentwise Euclidean sense. By
[[lem-chart-independence-of-c-r-smoothness]], this condition is independent of
the chosen charts: if one such representative is $C^r$, then every one is, so
"some charts" may be read as "any charts". A map is **$C^r$ on an open set**
$W\subseteq M$ when it is continuous on $W$ and $C^r$ at every point of $W$. A
map that is $C^r$ for every finite $r$ — equivalently $C^\infty$ — is called
**smooth**; the term **$C^r$ map between smooth manifolds** is reserved for the
case where $F$ is continuous and the representative condition holds at every
point of $M$.
Assuming $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, every second countable space is separable.

A topological space $X$ is **separable** if some at most countable subset $D\subseteq X$ is dense in $X$ ([[def-dense-top]], [[def-countable]]). Equivalently, every nonempty open subset of $X$ meets $D$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
geodesics, their maximal domains $I_{q,v}$ and the exponential maps
$\exp_q$ be those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Fix
$p\in M$. Write $\pi:TM\to M$ for the bundle projection.

**(a) Smoothness of the joint map.** The set
$$\mathcal D:=\{(q,v)\in TM:\ 1\in I_{q,v}\}\subseteq TM$$
is open in $TM$, and the **joint exponential map**
$$\Phi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M\times M,\qquad \Phi(q,v):=(q,\exp_q v),$$
is smooth.

**(b) Differential at $(p,0)$.** The differential $d\Phi_{(p,0)}$ is an
isomorphism. Explicitly, fix a smooth chart $(U,x)$ around $p$; it induces
the chart $(TU,Tx)$ of $TM$ and the product chart $(U\times U,x\times x)$ of
$M\times M$, and under the induced identifications
$T_{(p,0)}(TM)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ and
$T_{(p,p)}(M\times M)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ one has
$$d\Phi_{(p,0)}(u,w)=(u,\ u+w)\qquad\text{for all }u,w\in T_pM .$$

**(c) Diffeomorphism and two-point inverse.** There are open neighborhoods
$V\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $(p,0)$ and $W\subseteq M\times M$ of $(p,p)$ such
that $\Phi|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Moreover $V$ can be chosen
product-like: there are a chart $(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$, a radius
$r>0$ and a velocity radius $\rho>0$ such that, writing $B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb
R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$,
$$V=\bigl\{(q,v):\ q\in x^{-1}(B_r),\ \text{the coordinate components of }v\text{ in }(TU,Tx)\text{ lie in }B_\rho\bigr\},$$
and there is $s\in(0,r)$ with $x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$.
Consequently the velocity map
$$v:W\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (q,r)\longmapsto v(q,r):=\text{the vector with }(q,v(q,r))\in V,\ \Phi(q,v(q,r))=(q,r),$$
is well defined and smooth, and $\exp_q\bigl(v(q,r)\bigr)=r$ for all
$(q,r)\in W$.

**(d) Lipschitz bound for the two-point inverse.** On every pair
$x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$ as in (c) there is a constant
$\Lambda\ge 0$ such that, for all $q,r\in x^{-1}(B_s)$,
$$|v(q,r)|_x\le\Lambda\,\bigl|x(q)-x(r)\bigr|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $|v|_x$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate components of
$v$ and $v(q,q)=0$. In particular $|v(q,r)|_x\le 2\Lambda s$ on this pair.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$. For every $x\in M$ there is an open
neighborhood $B$ of $x$, a strictly convex normal ball satisfying the
hypotheses of [[thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone]] with base point
$x$, such that, writing $J_B(x)$, $I_B(x)\subseteq B$ for the endpoints in
$B$ of future causal, respectively future timelike, curves with image in
$B$ starting at $x$, and $\mathcal C^+,\mathcal T^+,\mathcal N^+$ for the
future causal or zero, future timelike, and future null nonzero vectors of
$\exp_x^{-1}(B)$:

**(a)** $J_B(x)=\exp_x(\mathcal C^+)$, $I_B(x)=\exp_x(\mathcal T^+)$, and
$J_B(x)\setminus(I_B(x)\cup\{x\})=\exp_x(\mathcal N^+)$;

**(b)** $J_B(x)$ and $J_B(x)\setminus I_B(x)$ are closed in $B$ and
$I_B(x)$ is open in $B$;

**(c)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to B$
with $\gamma(0)=\gamma(1)=x$;

**(d) corner smoothing.** if $\gamma:[0,1]\to B$ is future causal with
$\gamma(0)=x$ and there is $t_0$ at which $\gamma'(t_0)$ is future

**(e) closed relation at fixed base.** if $q_n\in J_B(x)$ and

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\in J^+(q)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Write $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ for the image of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{R}$
under the canonical embedding $q \mapsto \hat q$ ([[lem-rat-embeds-dense]]), the
set usually written $\mathbb{Q}$ once the identification is made, and put
$X := \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ for the irrationals. Then:

1. $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$, that is,
   $\overline{\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}} = \mathbb{R}$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]);
2. $X$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$;
3. every nonempty open subset of $\mathbb{R}$ is uncountable
   ([[def-countable]]).

Claim 2 is not a symmetry of claim 1: the rationals are dense because they are
*constructed* to approximate, whereas the irrationals are dense because there are
too many points in any interval for a countable set to exhaust it, which is why
claim 3 is proved alongside and used for it.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), and let
$t$ be the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]]. Then
there exist a smooth function $T:M\to\mathbb R$ and, with $\nabla T$ the
gradient of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], the
following hold.

**(a)** $T$ is a temporal function in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (e): smooth,
$g(\nabla T,\nabla T)<0$ and $g(\nabla T,N)>0$ everywhere.

**(b)** Every level set $S_c:=T^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is a Cauchy
hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clauses (a)
and (c)): it is a spacelike embedded hypersurface and every inextendible
causal curve meets it in exactly one parameter value. In particular $T$ is
surjective.

**(c)** Along every inextendible future-directed causal curve
$T\to+\infty$, and along every inextendible past-directed causal curve
$T\to-\infty$.

**(d)** The vector field $X:=\nabla T/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$ is smooth,
future-directed timelike, satisfies $X(T)=1$, and is complete
([[def-complete-vector-field]]): every maximal integral curve of $X$ is
defined on all of $\mathbb R$, so by
[[prop-a-vector-field-is-complete-if-and-only-if-its-flow-is-global]] its
flow $\Phi:\mathbb R\times M\to M$ is a global smooth flow
([[def-local-and-global-flow]]).

**(e)** The map $\Psi:\mathbb R\times S_0\to M$, $\Psi(s,z):=\Phi(s,z)$, is
a diffeomorphism and $T(\Psi(s,z))=s$ for all $(s,z)$; equivalently $M$ is
foliated by the Cauchy hypersurfaces $S_c$, each flow line meeting each level
exactly once.

**(f)** Put $\beta:=-1/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$, a smooth positive function, and
$h_T:=g+\beta\,dT\otimes dT$. Then $g=-\beta\,dT\otimes dT+h_T$;
$h_T(X,\cdot)=0$; and $h_T$ restricted to $\ker dT$ is a smooth Riemannian
metric, so the decomposition $T_pM=\mathbb RX_p\oplus\ker dT_p$ is
$g$-orthogonal with $g(X,X)=-\beta$. Consequently the pullback of $g$ by the
diffeomorphism $\Psi$ has no mixed terms,
$$\Psi^*g=-(\beta\circ\Psi)\,ds^2+h,\qquad h_{(s,z)}(v,w):=g_{\Phi(s,z)}\bigl((d\Phi_s)_zv,(d\Phi_s)_zw\bigr),$$
a sum of a negative definite one-dimensional form and the smooth family of
Riemannian metrics induced on the levels.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

**Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice** ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(A_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a family of at most countable sets
([[def-countable]]) indexed by $\mathbb{N}$. Then

$$U = \bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} A_n$$

is at most countable.

**The hypothesis $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is not decoration and it is not removable.**
It is spent at exactly one step, step 3.1 below, where one surjection
$\mathbb{N} \to A_n$ is selected for every $n$ at once. Each $A_n$ has such
surjections, in general many of them, and the countability assumption provides no
rule for singling one out. Without some choice principle the theorem is not
available at all: ZF alone does not prove it, **conditionally on the consistency
of ZF**, as recorded on the later foundations page
`symmetric-collapse-and-ultrafilter-free-models-examples`. The
consistency hypothesis is not a formality and cannot be dropped: the separation
rests on an external independence result that this library quotes rather than
proves, and it cannot be stated without it.

Recall that a natural number is a von Neumann natural
([[def-natural-numbers]]): $0 = \varnothing$ and $\sigma(n) = n \cup \{n\}$, so
that

$$n = \{\, m \in \mathbb{N} : m < n \,\} = \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$$

is itself the set of its predecessors. Here $<$ is the order of
[[def-nat-order]], which is defined additively, so the displayed identity is a
theorem and not a convention: it is [[lem-nat-order-is-membership]], proved
immediately above. Let $A$ be a set, and let $\approx$ be equinumerosity
([[def-equinumerous]]).

- $A$ is **finite** if $A \approx n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
- $A$ is **countably infinite** if $A \approx \mathbb{N}$.
- $A$ is **at most countable** if it is finite or countably infinite.
- $A$ is **uncountable** if it is not at most countable.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: (The set $D$.) Choose a countable dense subset $S_0\subseteq\bar j(\Sigma)$ ([L2]) and set $D_0:=S_0$. Recursively, given the countable set $D_n$, choose by Countable Choice a basis $(e_1(x),\dots,e_4(x))$ of $T_xQ$ for every $x\in D_n$, form $V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}$ as in the statement, and define $D_{n+1}$ by adding all points $\exp_x(v)$ with $x\in D_n$, $v\in V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}$ timelike and $\exp_x(v)$ defined. Each $D_{n+1}$ is countable, being the image of the countable set $D_n\times(V_x^{\mathrm{rat}})_{x}$; hence $D:=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}D_n$ is countable by [L6]. Since $D_0\subseteq D$, claim (a) holds.

(Chains of small timelike chords in a member.) Let $p\in Q$; choose $\alpha$ with $p\in Q_\alpha$ and write $p'=(\pi|_{U_\alpha})^{-1}(p)\in U_\alpha$. By [L5] there are $x_1\in j_0(\Sigma)$ and $t_1\in\mathbb R$ with $p'=\Phi(t_1,x_1)$, and the map $t\mapsto\Phi(t,x_1)$ is a timelike curve. Choose $n$ large enough that for each $j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ the subsegment $\Phi([\frac{j-1}{n}t_1,\frac{j}{n}t_1],x_1)$ is contained in a strictly convex normal ball $B_j$ around $z_{j-1}:=\Phi(\frac{j-1}{n}t_1,x_1)$ (finitely many such balls around the points of the compact segment cover it, and refining the subdivision makes each subsegment lie in one of them). Put $z_j:=\Phi(\frac{j}{n}t_1,x_1)$ for $j=0,\dots,n$, so that $z_0=x_1\in j_0(\Sigma)$ and $z_n=p'$. Transport the chain to $Q$ by the isometry $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ and keep the notation $z_j$ for the images in $Q_\alpha$; exponential maps and chronological relations correspond under this isometry ([[lem-gr-universal-development]] clause (d)). Each pair satisfies $z_{j-1}\ll z_j$ (they are distinct points of the timelike curve $t\mapsto\Phi(t,x_1)$), and the subsegment between them lies in $B_j$, so by [L4] there is a timelike $w_j\in T_{z_{j-1}}U_\alpha$ with $\exp_{z_{j-1}}(w_j)=z_j$.

(Propagation of rational approximations along a chain.) Let $O\subseteq U_\alpha$ be an open neighbourhood of $p'$ and fix a chart at $p'$. We show by induction on $j=0,\dots,n$: for every $\eta>0$ there is $d_j\in D\cap U_\alpha$ with $|d_j-z_j|<\eta$ in the chart. For $j=0$ this is the density of $S_0$ in $j_0(\Sigma)$ (step 1.1, transported by the diffeomorphism $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$). For the step, suppose $d_{j-1}\in D\cap U_\alpha$ is close to $z_{j-1}$. By continuity of the two-point inverse ([L3]) the exact inverse velocity $v(d_{j-1},z_j)$ (defined as soon as $d_{j-1}$ and $z_j$ lie in a common strictly convex normal ball, which holds for $d_{j-1}$ close enough to $z_{j-1}$) converges, as $d_{j-1}\to z_{j-1}$, to $w_j$; in particular for $d_{j-1}$ close enough it is timelike, by openness of the timelike cone [L4]. Choose $v\in V^{\mathrm{rat}}_{d_{j-1}}$ close to $v(d_{j-1},z_j)$; then $v$ is timelike, $\exp_{d_{j-1}}(v)$ is defined (the exponential domain is open, [L3]), and by the smoothness of the exponential and its Lipschitz bounds on a compact chart ([L3]) the point $d_j':=\exp_{d_{j-1}}(v)$ is as close to $z_j$ as desired, because the two terms $d(\exp_{d_{j-1}}(v),\exp_{d_{j-1}}(v(d_{j-1},z_j)))$ and $d(\exp_{d_{j-1}}(v(d_{j-1},z_j)),z_j)=d(d_{j-1},z_j)$ can both be made small: the first because $v$ approximates the exact inverse velocity and the exponential is Lipschitz on the compact chart, the second because the chain steps are small and $d_{j-1}$ is close to $z_{j-1}$. ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix the data of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$, a
matter sector with initial data $\psi_0$, and constants $\Lambda,\kappa$.
Write $Z_0:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ and let $j_0:\Sigma\to Z_0$,
$j_0(x):=(x,0)$.

**(a) The set-sized family.** Let $\mathcal X$ be the collection of all
tuples $(U,g,N,\psi)$ such that $U\subseteq Z_0$ is an open neighbourhood of
$j_0(\Sigma)$ in $Z_0$, $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $U$, $N$ a time
orientation and $\psi$ matter fields of the sector on $U$, and
$(U,g,N,j_0,\psi)$ is a development of the data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a). Then
$\mathcal X$ is a set, and it is nonempty provided at least one development
of the data exists.

**(b) Identifications.** For $\alpha=(U_\alpha,g_\alpha,N_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$
and $\beta\in\mathcal X$ let $(U_{\alpha\beta},\varphi_{\alpha\beta})$ be
their maximal common development, regarded as a subset of $U_\alpha$
([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]], [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]];
in the convention of the definition it is realised inside the first member).
Let $Z:=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}U_\alpha$ and let $\sim$ be the
equivalence relation on $Z$ **generated** by the relations
$x\sim\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(x)$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal X$ and
$x\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ (a finite chain of such steps, in either order).
Then the classes of two points $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$ coincide if and
only if $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)$.

**(c) The quotient.** Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi$. Then
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset
$Q_\alpha:=\pi(U_\alpha)$, the family $\{Q_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}$
covers $Q$, and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(d) Structure.** $Q$ is Hausdorff and locally Euclidean and carries a
unique smooth atlas (unique in the sense of maximal atlases compatible with
the charts below) making all maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms onto open
subsets, together with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, a time orientation
$\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ such that every $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ is an
isometry onto its image preserving time orientation and matter fields, and
such that $\bar j:=\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ (independent of $\alpha$) is a
common embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data $(h,K,\psi_0)$. The field
equations hold on $Q$, and every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in
$Q$ meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value. Hence
$(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ satisfies every clause of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a) except possibly
the second countability of the underlying manifold; if $Q$ is second
countable then it is a development of the data.

**(e) Universality.** Every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data
admits a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.

**Data.** Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, so that $\Sigma$ is
Hausdorff, second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$,
let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, and let a **matter sector** be specified
as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a finite list of tensor types
$r_1,\dots,r_s$, a smooth **stress-energy construction** $T(g,\psi)$, a smooth
covariant symmetric $2$-tensor field built from a Lorentzian metric $g$ and
fields $\psi=(\psi^1,\dots,\psi^s)$ of the listed types on a four-manifold
carrying $\Sigma$, and a system $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that in every chart the
combined system for $(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] is a first-order quasilinear
symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on shell. Let smooth **matter initial data**
$\psi_0$ on $\Sigma$ be given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$

$\Sigma$, with $n$ the future unit normal and $T$ determined by $(h,K,\psi_0)$.
The concrete sectors used later in this batch are the vacuum sector ($s=0$,
$T=0$), the scalar-field sector ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), the
strict barotropic perfect-fluid sector ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]])
and the geodesic-dust sector ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); no other sector is
asserted here.

$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);

   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));

uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

A topological space $X$ is **second countable** when its topology has a basis $\mathcal B$ that is at most countable ([[def-topology-basis-subbasis]], [[def-countable]]). Thus every open set is a union of members of one at most countable family $\mathcal B$.

Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, let $F:M\to N$ be a map, let $p\in M$ and
let $r\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$.
For $m,q\in\mathbb N_0$ and an open set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, a map
$g:E\to\mathbb R^q$ is **of class $C^r$** as follows. When $m=0$, every such
map is declared $C^r$. When $m\ge1$, each component $g_l$ with $l<q$ must be
$C^r$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]; when $q=0$ this
component condition is vacuous.
Suppose $F$ is continuous at $p$. Then $F$ is **of class $C^r$ at $p$** when
there are smooth charts $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ at $p$ and $(V,\psi)$ of $N$ at
$F(p)$ with $F(U)\subseteq V$ such that the coordinate representative

$$\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(U)\longrightarrow\psi(V)$$

([[def-coordinate-representation-of-a-map]]) is of class $C^r$ on a
neighbourhood of $\varphi(p)$ in this componentwise Euclidean sense. By
[[lem-chart-independence-of-c-r-smoothness]], this condition is independent of
the chosen charts: if one such representative is $C^r$, then every one is, so
"some charts" may be read as "any charts". A map is **$C^r$ on an open set**
$W\subseteq M$ when it is continuous on $W$ and $C^r$ at every point of $W$. A
map that is $C^r$ for every finite $r$ — equivalently $C^\infty$ — is called
**smooth**; the term **$C^r$ map between smooth manifolds** is reserved for the
case where $F$ is continuous and the representative condition holds at every
point of $M$.
Assuming $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, every second countable space is separable.

A topological space $X$ is **separable** if some at most countable subset $D\subseteq X$ is dense in $X$ ([[def-dense-top]], [[def-countable]]). Equivalently, every nonempty open subset of $X$ meets $D$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
geodesics, their maximal domains $I_{q,v}$ and the exponential maps
$\exp_q$ be those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Fix
$p\in M$. Write $\pi:TM\to M$ for the bundle projection.

**(a) Smoothness of the joint map.** The set
$$\mathcal D:=\{(q,v)\in TM:\ 1\in I_{q,v}\}\subseteq TM$$
is open in $TM$, and the **joint exponential map**
$$\Phi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M\times M,\qquad \Phi(q,v):=(q,\exp_q v),$$
is smooth.

**(b) Differential at $(p,0)$.** The differential $d\Phi_{(p,0)}$ is an
isomorphism. Explicitly, fix a smooth chart $(U,x)$ around $p$; it induces
the chart $(TU,Tx)$ of $TM$ and the product chart $(U\times U,x\times x)$ of
$M\times M$, and under the induced identifications
$T_{(p,0)}(TM)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ and
$T_{(p,p)}(M\times M)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ one has
$$d\Phi_{(p,0)}(u,w)=(u,\ u+w)\qquad\text{for all }u,w\in T_pM .$$

**(c) Diffeomorphism and two-point inverse.** There are open neighborhoods
$V\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $(p,0)$ and $W\subseteq M\times M$ of $(p,p)$ such
that $\Phi|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Moreover $V$ can be chosen
product-like: there are a chart $(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$, a radius
$r>0$ and a velocity radius $\rho>0$ such that, writing $B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb
R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$,
$$V=\bigl\{(q,v):\ q\in x^{-1}(B_r),\ \text{the coordinate components of }v\text{ in }(TU,Tx)\text{ lie in }B_\rho\bigr\},$$
and there is $s\in(0,r)$ with $x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$.
Consequently the velocity map
$$v:W\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (q,r)\longmapsto v(q,r):=\text{the vector with }(q,v(q,r))\in V,\ \Phi(q,v(q,r))=(q,r),$$
is well defined and smooth, and $\exp_q\bigl(v(q,r)\bigr)=r$ for all
$(q,r)\in W$.

**(d) Lipschitz bound for the two-point inverse.** On every pair
$x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$ as in (c) there is a constant
$\Lambda\ge 0$ such that, for all $q,r\in x^{-1}(B_s)$,
$$|v(q,r)|_x\le\Lambda\,\bigl|x(q)-x(r)\bigr|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $|v|_x$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate components of
$v$ and $v(q,q)=0$. In particular $|v(q,r)|_x\le 2\Lambda s$ on this pair.

metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$. For every $x\in M$ there is an open
neighborhood $B$ of $x$, a strictly convex normal ball satisfying the
hypotheses of [[thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone]] with base point
$x$, such that, writing $J_B(x)$, $I_B(x)\subseteq B$ for the endpoints in
$B$ of future causal, respectively future timelike, curves with image in
$B$ starting at $x$, and $\mathcal C^+,\mathcal T^+,\mathcal N^+$ for the
future causal or zero, future timelike, and future null nonzero vectors of
$\exp_x^{-1}(B)$:

**(a)** $J_B(x)=\exp_x(\mathcal C^+)$, $I_B(x)=\exp_x(\mathcal T^+)$, and
$J_B(x)\setminus(I_B(x)\cup\{x\})=\exp_x(\mathcal N^+)$;

**(b)** $J_B(x)$ and $J_B(x)\setminus I_B(x)$ are closed in $B$ and
$I_B(x)$ is open in $B$;

**(c)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to B$
with $\gamma(0)=\gamma(1)=x$;

**(d) corner smoothing.** if $\gamma:[0,1]\to B$ is future causal with
$\gamma(0)=x$ and there is $t_0$ at which $\gamma'(t_0)$ is future
timelike, then $\gamma(1)\in I_B(x)$;

**(e) closed relation at fixed base.** if $q_n\in J_B(x)$ and
$q_n\to q\in B$, then $q\in J_B(x)$; the same holds for the other two
sets of (a) in place of $J_B(x)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\in J^+(q)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Write $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ for the image of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{R}$
under the canonical embedding $q \mapsto \hat q$ ([[lem-rat-embeds-dense]]), the
set usually written $\mathbb{Q}$ once the identification is made, and put
$X := \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ for the irrationals. Then:

1. $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$, that is,
   $\overline{\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}} = \mathbb{R}$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]);
2. $X$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$;
3. every nonempty open subset of $\mathbb{R}$ is uncountable
   ([[def-countable]]).

Claim 2 is not a symmetry of claim 1: the rationals are dense because they are
*constructed* to approximate, whereas the irrationals are dense because there are
too many points in any interval for a countable set to exhaust it, which is why
claim 3 is proved alongside and used for it.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), and let
$t$ be the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]]. Then
there exist a smooth function $T:M\to\mathbb R$ and, with $\nabla T$ the
gradient of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], the
following hold.

**(a)** $T$ is a temporal function in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (e): smooth,
$g(\nabla T,\nabla T)<0$ and $g(\nabla T,N)>0$ everywhere.

**(b)** Every level set $S_c:=T^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is a Cauchy
hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clauses (a)
and (c)): it is a spacelike embedded hypersurface and every inextendible
causal curve meets it in exactly one parameter value. In particular $T$ is
surjective.

**(c)** Along every inextendible future-directed causal curve
$T\to+\infty$, and along every inextendible past-directed causal curve
$T\to-\infty$.

**(d)** The vector field $X:=\nabla T/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$ is smooth,
future-directed timelike, satisfies $X(T)=1$, and is complete
([[def-complete-vector-field]]): every maximal integral curve of $X$ is
defined on all of $\mathbb R$, so by
[[prop-a-vector-field-is-complete-if-and-only-if-its-flow-is-global]] its
flow $\Phi:\mathbb R\times M\to M$ is a global smooth flow
([[def-local-and-global-flow]]).

**(e)** The map $\Psi:\mathbb R\times S_0\to M$, $\Psi(s,z):=\Phi(s,z)$, is
a diffeomorphism and $T(\Psi(s,z))=s$ for all $(s,z)$; equivalently $M$ is
foliated by the Cauchy hypersurfaces $S_c$, each flow line meeting each level
exactly once.

**(f)** Put $\beta:=-1/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$, a smooth positive function, and
$h_T:=g+\beta\,dT\otimes dT$. Then $g=-\beta\,dT\otimes dT+h_T$;
$h_T(X,\cdot)=0$; and $h_T$ restricted to $\ker dT$ is a smooth Riemannian
metric, so the decomposition $T_pM=\mathbb RX_p\oplus\ker dT_p$ is
$g$-orthogonal with $g(X,X)=-\beta$. Consequently the pullback of $g$ by the
diffeomorphism $\Psi$ has no mixed terms,
$$\Psi^*g=-(\beta\circ\Psi)\,ds^2+h,\qquad h_{(s,z)}(v,w):=g_{\Phi(s,z)}\bigl((d\Phi_s)_zv,(d\Phi_s)_zw\bigr),$$
a sum of a negative definite one-dimensional form and the smooth family of
Riemannian metrics induced on the levels.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

**Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice** ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(A_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a family of at most countable sets
([[def-countable]]) indexed by $\mathbb{N}$. Then

$$U = \bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} A_n$$

is at most countable.

**The hypothesis $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is not decoration and it is not removable.**
It is spent at exactly one step, step 3.1 below, where one surjection
$\mathbb{N} \to A_n$ is selected for every $n$ at once. Each $A_n$ has such
surjections, in general many of them, and the countability assumption provides no
rule for singling one out. Without some choice principle the theorem is not
available at all: ZF alone does not prove it, **conditionally on the consistency
of ZF**, as recorded on the later foundations page
`symmetric-collapse-and-ultrafilter-free-models-examples`. The
consistency hypothesis is not a formality and cannot be dropped: the separation
rests on an external independence result that this library quotes rather than
proves, and it cannot be stated without it.

Recall that a natural number is a von Neumann natural
([[def-natural-numbers]]): $0 = \varnothing$ and $\sigma(n) = n \cup \{n\}$, so
that

$$n = \{\, m \in \mathbb{N} : m < n \,\} = \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$$

is itself the set of its predecessors. Here $<$ is the order of
[[def-nat-order]], which is defined additively, so the displayed identity is a
theorem and not a convention: it is [[lem-nat-order-is-membership]], proved
immediately above. Let $A$ be a set, and let $\approx$ be equinumerosity
([[def-equinumerous]]).

- $A$ is **finite** if $A \approx n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
- $A$ is **countably infinite** if $A \approx \mathbb{N}$.
- $A$ is **at most countable** if it is finite or countably infinite.
- $A$ is **uncountable** if it is not at most countable.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix the data of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$,
one fixed admissible covariant matter model with its complete smooth Cauchy
data $d$, and constants $\Lambda,\kappa$. The model and its complete data,
including all required initial derivatives and prescribed fields on empty
regions, are fixed throughout. Assume the supplied complete-data local
existence and geometric uniqueness hypotheses apply on every spacelike
restart surface occurring in comparisons, as required by that definition.
Assume that at least one development of these data exists.
Write $Z_0:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ and let $j_0:\Sigma\to Z_0$,
$j_0(x):=(x,0)$.

**(a) The set-sized family.** Let $\mathcal X$ be the collection of all
tuples $(U,g,N,\psi)$ such that $U\subseteq Z_0$ is an open neighbourhood of
$j_0(\Sigma)$ in $Z_0$, $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $U$, $N$ a time
orientation and $\psi$ matter fields of the sector on $U$, and
$(U,g,N,j_0,\psi)$ is a development of the data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a). Then
$\mathcal X$ is a set, and it is nonempty provided at least one development
of the data exists.

**(b) Identifications.** For $\alpha=(U_\alpha,g_\alpha,N_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$
and $\beta\in\mathcal X$ let $(U_{\alpha\beta},\varphi_{\alpha\beta})$ be
their maximal common development, regarded as a subset of $U_\alpha$
([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]], [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]];
in the convention of the definition it is realised inside the first member).
Let $Z:=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}U_\alpha$ and let $\sim$ be the
equivalence relation on $Z$ **generated** by the relations
$x\sim\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(x)$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal X$ and
$x\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ (a finite chain of such steps, in either order).
Then the classes of two points $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$ coincide if and
only if $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)$.

**(c) The quotient.** Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi$. Then
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset
$Q_\alpha:=\pi(U_\alpha)$, the family $\{Q_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}$
covers $Q$, and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(d) Structure.** $Q$ is a Hausdorff, second countable smooth four-manifold and carries a
unique smooth atlas (unique in the sense of maximal atlases compatible with
the charts below) making all maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms onto open
subsets, together with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, a time orientation
$\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ such that every $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ is an
isometry onto its image preserving time orientation and matter fields, and
such that $\bar j:=\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ (independent of $\alpha$) is a
common embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data $(h,K,d)$. The field
equations hold on $Q$, and every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in
$Q$ meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value. Consequently
$(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ is a development of the data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a).
The representative $\bar N$ is chosen to determine the common future cones;
it need not equal the pushforward of each representative $N_\alpha$.

**(e) Universality.** Every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data
admits a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
